item.title: Penn State Cancels Classes, Centre County Schools to Be Closed on Monday
item.description: Penn State's University Park campus and all Centre County school districts will be closed on Monday because of the major winter storm blanketing the area. The university has canceled classes, activity and most work from 5 a.m. Monday until 5 a.m. Tuesday. Only employees designated as performing essential services should report during that time. item.title: Scenes From a Snowy Day in Centre County
item.description: A major winter storm that stretched from New Mexico to New England brought heavy snowfall to Centre County throughout the day on Sunday. Snow started in the area at about 1:30 a.m. and by Sunday afternoon 8 to 12 inches had accumulated around the county, with the storm continuing into Sunday night. A winter storm warning was in effect until 1 p.m. Monday. item.title: Which Centre County Locations Saw the Most Snow During Sunday’s Storm? See the Reported Totals
item.description: Parts of Centre County saw a foot or more of snow on Sunday in what looks to have been the area's biggest storm in more than five years, according to totals reported to and by the National Weather Service at State College. The largest accumulation in the county was reported in Port Matilda, which received 15.5 inches. Unionville had the second-most at 14 inches. item.title: ‘Gimme Shelter’ Benefit Concert to Support Housing Security in Centre Region
item.description: This story originally appeared in The Centre County Gazette. item.title: Centre County Schools Operating on 2-Hour Delays for Tuesday
item.description: The winter storm that brought about a foot of snow to much of Centre County on Sunday is continuing to cause disruptions. State College, Bald Eagle, Bellefonte, Penns Valley and Philipsburg-Osceola school districts will be operating on two-hour delays on Tuesday, each district announced late Monday afternoon. item.title: State College Demonstrators Protest ICE, Call for Justice in Fatal Minneapolis Shooting of Alex Pretti
item.description: More than 100 people gathered Monday night in front of Penn State’s Old Main to protest Immigration and Customs Enforcement operations and demand accountability in the recent death of Alex Pretti, a Minneapolis man killed by federal agents earlier this week. The demonstration drew students and community members and included speeches, a vigil and a march through downtown State College.
